item.miehex.miehex_ruined_circles_nether: Nether Ruined Spell Circle Structure Soul
item.miehex.miehex_ruined_circles_shulk_: Deep Dark Ruined Spell Circle Structure Soul
hexcasting.mishap.invalid_value.class.sl: A number in a suitable range
hexcasting.mishap.invalid_value.class.re: A coordinate with close ties to the deceased
miehex.entry.miehex_patterns.desc: New patterns added by the Hexcasting Major Pack
miehex.entry.ideas_world_entry.desc: Creating a portal to another realm of consciousness
miehex.entry.ideas_world_entry.desc1: I discovered that by gathering some special materials together and using a Biome Soul as a guide, a special portal to a wonderful world can be created. That world is vast and empty, seemingly dormant for a long time. I arbitrarily want to call it the Ideas World. Perhaps I could build my own Eden there.
miehex.entry.ideas_world_entry.desc2: The entrance to the Ideas World seems to be a one-time consumable.
miehex.entry.ideas_world_entry.desc3: A special woven item embroidered with complex spells. When right-clicked, it teleports the entity above it to the corresponding Ideas World for the current dimension. Unfortunately, the return journey is not convenient.
miehex.entry.biome_symbols.desc: I understand that matter can affect consciousness, and consciousness can act upon matter... Every tree, flower, and plant in our world has its own will. Using the Pure Allay, a wonderful material, the shadow of their consciousness can be traced - almost indistinguishable from their original consciousness. If we do this, Quenched Allay can be transformed into Biome Souls. If we then apply this 'Biome Soul' back to our environment, I can change the biome of that small area - artificially creating nature belonging to me.
miehex.entry.structure_symbols.desc: By modifying Biome Souls, Structure Souls can be crafted. This glittering and wonderful item, combined with special spells, can locate structures in the same dimension. Unfortunately, nature will only tell me the distance from a certain position to that structure. Nevertheless, there may still be a way to obtain the precise coordinates of structures.
miehex.entry.structure_symbols.example: Here I give only one crafting example, after all, there are many types of Structure Souls.
miehex.entry.pure_allay.desc: I once glimpsed the wonderful relationship between Allay and Media during the Greatness Awakening. I used an excellent method to temper the Allay and obtained Quenched Allay. But spells created by human hands can surely surpass the enlightenment given by nature. So I tried to collect the consciousness that Allay scatters, which was surprisingly easy. This may be because they are constantly changing, reorganizing, and disintegrating.
miehex.entry.pure_allay.entity_advice: Can only accept a list consisting of one entity. Consumes a small amount of media. Waits 10 seconds.
miehex.entry.pure_allay.block_advice: To be honest, the resulting material disappointed me. The so-called crystallization of pure spirituality turned out to be a rather illusory, fragile, and strange block. I call it Pure Allay Block. When the Pure Allay Block is broken, Pure Allay Shards can be obtained.
miehex.entry.pure_allay.shard_advice: The Pure Allay Shards don't seem to have any obvious use either. However, holding them always gives me a feeling of transparent enlightenment and rebirth. Perhaps I should try making some items with them.
miehex.entry.collect_consciousness.desc1: Separating consciousness is too extreme, too evil, too wasteful... Actually, there can be a simpler, kinder, and more economical way to use consciousness. Like 'Collect Consciousness' - as long as a living being still lives, its consciousness will operate continuously. During this process, some energy inevitably escapes.
miehex.entry.collect_consciousness.desc2: This escaping energy can be collected and used to create many things. Though insignificant compared to the consciousness subject, accumulated over time, it can also create miracles.
miehex.entry.collect_consciousness.side_: At the same time, due to the vibration of discrete consciousness aggregation on the subject's consciousness, those creatures will receive a certain amount of damage.
miehex.entry.all_in_one.desc: A staff capable of storing multiple iotas
miehex.entry.idea_blocks.desc: Blocks that embody the essence of other blocks
miehex.entry.idea.desc: The eternal templates of all things
miehex.advice.import_quine: This pattern returns a special pattern list that remains itself after a Hermes Strategy, perhaps this will have some good use.
miehex.advice.exchant_exchange: Accepts two item entity iotas, swaps their enchantments, or removes enchantments from one and adds them to another. Consumes 1 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.exchant_exchange.note: It seems this spell cannot be used to enchant books. Perhaps an 'empty' enchantment book should be used.
miehex.advice.list_insert: Inserts the iota at stack position 0 into the beginning or end of the list at stack position 1.
miehex.advice.all_in_one_pages: Sets the current page of the All-in-One Staff to the specified page number (starting from 1).
miehex.advice.all_in_one_read: Reads all iotas stored in the All-in-One Staff pages, returning them as a list (elements ordered by page number).
miehex.advice.all_eval: Executes the pattern list stored at the specified page of the All-in-One Staff (that page must store a list iota).
miehex.advice.all_record: Saves all iotas from the current All-in-One Staff as a list into the world. Can be read with 'Resurgence Meditation'.
miehex.advice.record_read: Reads the saved iota list from the world (saved by 'Monument Strategy'), pushing it to the stack top. Returns an empty list if nothing has been saved.
miehex.advice.all_in_one: Converts any iota without nested lists into a pattern, or converts such a pattern back into its original iota.
miehex.advice.easy_thrust: Accepts a list at position 0, a list at position 1, and a number at position 2. Inserts elements from the list at position 1 after the element at the given index in the list at position 0.
miehex.advice.easy_extract: Accepts a list and two numbers. Returns the sublist starting at the first number with length equal to the second number, and the remaining elements.
miehex.advice.cube_type: Accepts two position vectors and a string. Returns coordinates of all blocks in the cube with IDs matching the given string.
miehex.advice.cube_types: Accepts two position vectors and a list of strings. Returns coordinates of blocks whose IDs match any of the given strings.
miehex.advice.zone_entity/by_name: Accepts a position, maximum distance, and a string. Returns all entities with matching names within range.
miehex.advice.create_sapling: Places a sapling with the given block ID at the target position. Consumes 1 amethyst dust.
miehex.advice.create_sword: Gives the target player a media sword with Looting III and Unbreakable. Consumes 10 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.collect_consciousness: Accepts a list of living entities and a position. Collects their scattered consciousness energy, which will form a special block after some time.
miehex.advice.create_symbols: Gets the biome at the target position, converts 1 Pure Allay Shard in the offhand into 16 Biome Souls. Consumes 1 amethyst shard.
miehex.advice.change_biome: Consumes a Biome Soul from offhand to transform a small area around the target vector into the corresponding biome. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.idea_entry: Accepts a position vector and an integer between 0, 1, and 2. Consumes an Ideas World Entry from offhand. Teleports to the corresponding coordinates in that world.
miehex.advice.back_to_overworld: Accepts a player entity and teleports them to their overworld spawn point. Consumes 1 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.get_spawn: Returns the respawn point position vector.
miehex.advice.create_block/idea: Generates an Idea Block at the target position. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.idealized_block: Transforms the target block into its Idea Block form. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.locate: Accepts a position vector, consumes a Structure Soul from offhand, and returns the horizontal distance to the structure.
miehex.advice.push: Accepts a player entity and an iota. Places the iota in the player's staff stack and displays it in their crosshair for a time. Consumes 1 amethyst dust.
miehex.advice.crash: Accepts a player entity and ejects one of their consumed tapes from their mind. Consumes 1 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.inventory_control: Accepts two inventory indices and swaps the items at those slots. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.item_control: Accepts an inventory index or an item entity. Drops one item from the slot or fills empty slots with the item entity. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.expelliarmus: Accepts a living entity and makes it drop its held items. Consumes 1 amethyst shard.
miehex.advice.puzzle: Accepts a player and two inventory indices, swapping items at those slots. Consumes 1 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.get_target: Accepts an entity and returns the entity it wants to attack.
miehex.advice.anglebetweenvectors: Accepts two vectors and calculates the yaw and pitch angles (in radians) needed to point from the first to the second.
miehex.advice.anglebetweenscalar: Accepts two vectors and calculates the spatial angle between them (in radians).
miehex.advice.rotatevector: Accepts a vector, yaw angle, and pitch angle (all in radians). Rotates the vector around Y axis first, then X axis.
miehex.advice.great_connect: Accepts a list and creates a new staff casting environment inheriting the spell circle's caster, stack, raven thoughts, and lesser gateway destinations.
miehex.advice.chunkloader_permanent: Permanently force-loads the chunk at the given position. Consumes 1 amethyst shard.
miehex.advice.entity_anchor: Temporarily loads the chunk at the given position for about 15 seconds. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.lesser_gate: Accepts a vector within casting range. Uses it as the destination for Lesser Gateway Teleport until casting ends. Consumes 5 amethyst shards.
miehex.advice.lesser_gate/close: Accepts an entity and teleports it to the position set by Create Lesser Gateway. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.personal_media: Accepts a number and converts that many amethyst dust of media into personal media, with some minor loss.
miehex.advice.grow_up: Accepts a living entity and makes it fully grown immediately. Consumes 3 amethyst dust of media.
miehex.advice.memory: Memorizes the current stack and casting state. When cast again, overwrites the current stack and state with the memory and clears it.
miehex.advice.chat_listen: Accepts an iota. When the caster sends a chat message, that iota will be executed.
miehex.advice.get_structure: Accepts a position vector, consumes a Pure Allay Shard from offhand, and pleads with nature for a Structure Soul.
miehex.advice.idea_get: Consumes a small amount of media. Extracts base attributes (max health, speed, attack, armor) from the target entity into an empty idea.
miehex.advice.idea_summon: Summons a living entity at the target position based on the given idea, with attributes from the idea. Consumes (max health * 10 + speed * 1000 + attack * 100 + armor * 50) amethyst dust, minimum 1 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.idea_modify: Consumes a small amount of media. Modifies one attribute of an idea. Indices 1~4 correspond to: max health, speed, attack, armor.
miehex.page.idea_entry.teleport_rules: Teleport rules: $(br)- Overworld: $(bold)ideas_world_1$()$(br)- Nether: $(bold)ideas_world_0$()$(br)- End: $(bold)ideas_world_2$()$(br)Note: Unlike the spell to enter the Ideas World, the carpet does not generate a standing block at the destination. The teleported entity may fall into the void or get stuck in solid blocks.
miehex.advice.camera.desc: Peek requires an entity as target. The target can be a scroll with the pattern I marked, a Quenched Allay, other hexcasters, or myself. Consumes a small amount of media. Consumes 1 charged amethyst when the target is another hexcaster.
miehex.advice.destroy_components.desc1: Destroy Components is an extremely terrifying and destructive spell. It accepts a player entity and clears all 'special' tags from the item they are holding. If the main hand item doesn't match the target, it clears the offhand item.
miehex.advice.destroy_components.desc2: In particular, when clearing media like Focus that store iotas, it will fill them with a junk iota. The so-called special tags are what some people call NBT tags. Therefore, this spell can also remove enchantments, trinkets, and various potion effects from equipment. Consumes 30 charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.allay_mix.desc: Consumes all Quenched Allay Shards in the offhand, attempts to transform the target Allay into a Quenched Allay. The transformation probability is related to the number of shards. If successful, the generated entity is pushed to the stack top; if failed, it's probably due to inexperience.
miehex.advice.allay_move.desc: Accepts a Quenched Allay entity and a position vector. The Allay will then move towards this target.
miehex.advice.allay_casting.desc: Accepts a Quenched Allay entity, a number, and a list. Gives the Quenched Allay media equivalent to the given number of amethyst dust, and makes it execute the specified spell list. The Allay will cast after about 0.25 seconds.
miehex.advice.allay_stop.desc: Interrupts the next spell the target Allay would execute via Puppeteer Strategy and clears its casting state.
miehex.advice.function.desc: Packages the pattern list in the middle into a function iota, marked with a required parameter iota and a result iota after execution. It's worth mentioning that these don't have to be real return values and required iotas.
miehex.advice.function_check.desc: Before executing the pattern list in the function, it checks the second iota from the top of the stack (the first is the function). If that iota's type matches the required iota marked by the function, it removes that iota and then executes the list; otherwise, it does nothing.
miehex.advice.function_check_care.desc: Before executing the pattern list in the function, it checks the second iota from the top of the stack (the first is the function). If that iota is exactly the same as the required iota marked by the function, it removes that iota and then executes the list; otherwise, it does nothing.
miehex.advice.function_halt.desc: This pattern is a function-specialized version of 'Charon's Strategy'. Drawing it inside a function body will immediately terminate the current function execution and correctly return to the call site. If used outside a function, its effect is the same as a normal Charon's Strategy.
miehex.advice.block_var.desc: Gets the 'block variable' of the current function level. When a function is called, the passed parameters are automatically stored in the block variable of the current level. Returns Null if not inside a function.
miehex.advice.block_var_write.desc: Stores the iota at the top of the stack into the block variable of the current function level, overwriting the original parameter value. Can be used to update state during function execution. Can only be used inside functions.
miehex.advice.block_var_read.desc: Reads the block variable at the specified depth. Depth starts at 0, which is 0 when not in any function, then increases by 1 for each additional nesting level... This allows me to access variables from outer functions, implementing a feature similar to 'closures'. Can only be used inside functions.
miehex.advice.block_var_writes.desc: Writes the iota at the top of the stack to the block variable at the specified depth. Similar to 'Resolver Strategy', but allows modification of outer function variables. Can be confusing if used improperly, but that's the price of power.
miehex.advice.collect_consciousness.desc: Accepts a list of living entities and a position. Collects their escaping consciousness energy and concentrates it at that position. After some time, the accumulated consciousness energy at that position will form a special block.
miehex.entry.camera.desc1: I discovered that I can use consciousness stripping to inject a small piece of my consciousness into a pattern, then create a scroll with that pattern drawn on it. I can then use the 'Peek' spell to observe the surroundings near them at any time. In fact, I can also use this spell to observe the world through the eyes of Quenched Allays or even other hexcasters - a rather odd limitation is that when I observe the world through their eyes, I cannot see my original body. Nature truly imposes some strange restrictions...
miehex.entry.camera.desc2: In either case, my physical body will temporarily lose awareness of its surroundings until I cast the spell again on myself. $(br2) This experience is quite wonderful. I seem to have left my body, yet cannot touch anything. I simply observe quietly, listening. Nature doesn't seem to mind me borrowing the senses of other beings, but only if I pay the price of media for this prying. And for those hexcasters I peek at, they should learn how to protect their true names.
miehex.entry.omniscience.desc1: I succeeded. $(br2) Ten thousand portions of amethyst dust, and at last the Beauty deigned to glance my way.
miehex.entry.omniscience.desc2: I can feel the world I know breathing with me... Though my consciousness is fragmented, I know my power is greater than ever. $(br2) As long as I remain in this dimension, I can access any location and any entity within it - I shall know all... $(br2) Of course, only within this dimension. After all, I have left that part of myself there forever.
miehex.entry.omniscience.desc3: But what if I split more of my consciousness? What if all of me merges with nature?
miehex.entry.function.desc1: I discovered that function iotas are a very special type of iota. They are like specially packaged pattern list iotas, marked with required parameters and output, but cannot be executed with normal meta-runs. When executed, nothing happens, and they don't even pop from the stack. Only through some special patterns can they be executed when the required parameters are met.
miehex.entry.function.desc2: In exploring the mysteries of function iotas, I realized that merely packaging and matching is not enough. I needed a way to terminate early inside functions, and the ability to store temporary data within functions - like a stack, but without polluting the main stack. Thus, I found a way to utilize the 'user data' in the hexcraft image, creating several auxiliary patterns.
miehex.entry.function.desc3: These patterns together form a simple but practical 'lexical scope' system. While not yet rigorous, it is a great step forward for my hexcraft.
miehex.entry.mix_allay.desc1: A hexcaster named Whiteord created a spell to make Quenched Allays. This Allay variant has acquired casting abilities due to the incorporation of large amounts of Quenched Allay Shard, and is also easier for hexcasters to control - such cute little fellows! But why do they always hang their heads?
miehex.entry.mix_allay.desc2: A lovely and charming wonderful creature
miehex.entry.collect_consciousness_spell: Stripping consciousness is too extreme, too evil, too wasteful... In fact, there can be a simpler, kinder, and more economical way to use consciousness. For example, 'Collect Consciousness' - as long as a living being is still alive, its consciousness will operate continuously, and some energy will inevitably escape during this process.
Collecting this escaping energy can be used to create many things. While insignificant compared to the consciousness subject, accumulated over time, it can also create miracles.

At the same time, due to the vibration of discrete consciousness aggregation on the subject's consciousness, those creatures will receive a certain amount of damage. I have recorded the relevant recipes in other chapters.
miehex.entry.self_pat.desc1: I attempted a new consciousness-stripping ritual. Instead of sealing another's consciousness into a block, I merged a small piece of my own consciousness - a thought, a memory, or just a 'sense of presence' - into a pattern. The process was more painful than expected, with a piece of my life force being torn away, but I gained an anchor. A piece of my own consciousness, engraved into the pattern's veins.
miehex.entry.self_pat.desc2: The ritual requires a pattern iota as a carrier. When I sacrificed it along with my body, that small piece of consciousness would forever attach itself to the pattern's veins. I didn't lose any memories, but my body did become weaker - as if a small part of myself had forever left this physical shell. The pattern itself showed no special changes, but whenever I gazed at it, I always felt a strange sense of intimacy, as if it were looking back at me.
miehex.entry.self_pat.desc3: This marked pattern will become an extension of my consciousness. Drawing it on a scroll allows me to observe the surroundings through the scroll's 'eyes' from a distance via the Peek spell - regardless, I have left my mark on this world. Even if my body decays, my consciousness will live on in the media.
miehex.entry.self_pat.desc4: — Come to think of it, was Prometheus also sealed into a pattern in a similar way? Further, could these patterns I use already be someone else's 'eyes'?
miehex.entry.destroy_components.desc1: Destroy Components is an extremely terrifying and destructive spell. It accepts a player entity and clears all 'special' tags from the item they are holding. If the main hand item doesn't match the target, it clears the offhand item.
miehex.entry.destroy_components.desc2: In particular, when clearing media like Focus that store iotas, it will fill them with a junk iota. The so-called special tags are what some people call NBT tags. Therefore, this spell can also remove enchantments, trinkets, and various potion effects from equipment. Consumes 30 charged amethyst.
miehex.entry.spatial_imprint.desc1: I understand, I understand! $(br2) How merciful is this great Nature, bestowing this wonderful enlightenment again and again! $(br2) ... If using hexcraft is using one's own will to manipulate media to make requests of Nature, then my limited consciousness can only manipulate limited Nature, for consciousness trapped in slimy gray-white nerves can never reach true freedom.
miehex.entry.spatial_imprint.desc2: I seek liberation... I will elevate myself to eternity, strip my consciousness into a space imprint, and use the spatial imprint to directly merge my consciousness into the dimension itself. $(br2) I will further merge with my love, my teacher, my comrade, my enemy, my mother and father, which is of course the great and eternal Nature. I will know what It knows, which is all of this world. Oh great Nature, I offer a precious part of my consciousness to You, for it has always belonged to You...
miehex.entry.spatial_imprint.desc3: Ten thousand portions of amethyst dust, one attempt and adventure.
miehex.category.babel_tower.desc: Strangely, this knowledge doesn't seem to come from any ancient texts, but from another self-contained world. This world and that world are similar in underlying logic, but their upper-level structures are completely different. The strange mysteries within are difficult to summarize; here I merely sketch those impressive patterns, they are... dazzling...
miehex.advice.af_kcit.desc: Reduces the block update time at the specified coordinate vector by 1 tick, with a 1/64 chance to trigger a random tick. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.af_space.desc: Uses the first two vectors as diagonal vertex coordinates of a cube, moves blocks matching the blacklist/whitelist to the position offset by the third vector from their original position.
miehex.entry.af_great.desc1: Judges all blocks in the selected area. If the boolean is true, selects all blocks whose names are contained in the string list; if false, excludes all blocks whose names are contained in the string list. Moves qualifying blocks by the offset vector represented by the third vector and clears the original area. $(br2) Records the total number of blocks moved as a, and the total number of blocks removed as b. Consumes (Math.log10(a) + 1)² * 100000 + b * 10 millionths of an amethyst dust worth of media.
miehex.advice.af_reflection.desc: Under certain conditions, cancels damage received by the caster and reflects it back to its source.
miehex.entry.af_great.desc2: Gives the caster a 1-second reflection effect. During reflection, all damage is canceled. After the reflection effect ends, enters a 6-second cooldown. Using it again during reflection or cooldown will give the caster Wither status. $(br2) However, if damage is received from another entity during the reflection period, the damage will be reflected back to the original entity and the cooldown will be canceled. Consumes a small amount of media.
miehex.advice.af_focus.desc: If the second parameter is a vector, redirects the entity's velocity to the direction of the specified vector, preserving its speed. If the second parameter is an entity, swaps the velocities of the two entities.
miehex.entry.af_great.desc3: If the second parameter is a number, uses current world time plus this number of ticks as the return time, records the entity's current velocity, then sets the entity's velocity to zero. When the return time is reached, adds back the recorded velocity. $(br2) If released again during the delay period, records the entity's current velocity and adds it to the recorded value, and updates the return time to this return time.
miehex.advice.af_grid.desc: Changes the scale size of the hexcraft grid, minimum value is 0.5, maximum value is 4.0.
miehex.advice.af_tags.desc: If the boolean is True or False, adds or removes string tags starting with T_; if null, judges whether the entity has the specified tag. If the string is empty, uses a glow effect instead of string tags.
miehex.advice.af_yaw.desc: Makes the specified entity look at the specified coordinate vector.
miehex.advice.af_ride.desc: Makes entity.1 ride entity.2. If the two are already in a mutual riding state, it will be removed. When the riding target is some special entities, dangerous results may occur.
miehex.advice.af_high.desc: Adds the specified value to the entity's y-coordinate, preserving its velocity.
miehex.advice.af_control.desc: Sets entity.2 as entity.1's attack target. Consumes (minimum of the two entities' current health) * 1,000 media points.
miehex.advice.af_simulation.desc: Deals damage to an entity from a virtual entity with the specified name, with the value being the specified positive integer. The cumulative damage to the same entity cannot exceed four points. Consumes 100 media points.
miehex.advice.af_uncrafting.desc: Disassembles the specified item entity into dropped items. Randomly selects a crafting recipe for the specified item, and returns each raw material with a 4/5 ~ 1/5 probability based on common, uncommon, rare, and epic rarity. Consumes 10,000 media points.
miehex.advice.af_gravity.desc: Sets the entity's gravity. Default value is 8, zero means no gravity, negative values mean gravity direction is upward. If the value is between 0-8, consumes 100 media points; greater than 8 is (num - 8) * 10000 points, less than 0 is num² * 10000 points.
miehex.advice.af_arrow.desc: Summons a gravity-ignoring spectral arrow at the specified coordinate vector with base damage equal to the specified value. num is an integer between 1-5. Pushes an entity iota representing the arrow into the stack. Consumes num² * 1,000 media points.
miehex.advice.af_tear.desc: Tears the specified entity in the opposite direction of its current velocity, and calculates consumption based on the difference in velocity magnitude before and after tearing.
miehex.entry.af_spell.desc1: Records the entity's current velocity as v, then gives the entity a velocity in the direction of the specified vector with magnitude equal to its magnitude, and performs tearing. $(br2) During tearing, deals damage equal to the square of the smaller value between |v| and |the component of vec in the opposite direction of v|. If the difference between the magnitude of the velocity after tearing and |v| is greater than 0.1, consumes (|vec + v| - |v|) * 30,000 media points, otherwise consumes 100 media points.
miehex.advice.af_let_in.desc: Stores the iota in the world's data with the specified number or string as ID. If the iota is null, removes the entry with the corresponding ID.
miehex.advice.af_let_read.desc: Limits the readable count of the specified ID entry and increases its readable count by num. The entry will be removed after being read the specified number of times. Returns the remaining readable count.
miehex.advice.af_let_out.desc: Returns the iota of the corresponding ID entry. If the specified ID is not used, returns null. If the entry has a limited readable count, decreases the readable count by one.
miehex.advice.af_echo.desc: Runs the $(thing)pattern list/$ at the top of the stack the specified number of times. The $(thing)results/$ of the runs will be returned to the $(thing)stack/$ .
miehex.advice.af_world.desc: Returns the name of the current dimension.
miehex.advice.af_found.desc: Judges whether there is a block with the specified name in the cube centered at the specified coordinate vector, with a plane side length of 2 * num, Y-axis less than or equal to the specified block, and greater than or equal to -64. Not limited by casting range.
miehex.advice.af_get_entity.desc: Returns the non-player entity at the specified coordinate vector.
miehex.advice.af_zone_block.desc: Returns a list of positions of all block entities within the range centered at the specified coordinate vector with the specified value as radius.
miehex.advice.af_get_tag.desc: $(br)Returns a list of all tags of the specified item entity, or the item in the specified slot, or the block at the specified coordinate vector, or the item with the specified name, or the specified mote.
miehex.advice.af_has_tag.desc: $(br)Judges whether the specified item entity, or the item in the specified slot, or the block at the specified coordinate vector, or the item with the specified name, or the specified mote contains the specified tag.
miehex.advice.af_id_write.desc: Writes the top iota of the stack to the $(l:patterns/readwrite#hexcasting:local)$(thing)Raven's Thought/$ with the given number as the sequence number.
miehex.advice.af_id_read.desc: Copies the iota from the $(l:patterns/readwrite#hexcasting:local)$(thing)Raven's Thought/$ with the given number as the sequence number to the top of the stack.
miehex.advice.af_num_read.desc: Copies the iota of the $(l:patterns/hexcasting#autumnfloods:slot)$(thing)specified slot/$ item and pushes it to the top of the stack. Returns null if the specified slot has no readable iota.
miehex.advice.af_num_write.desc: Removes the top element of the stack. If the $(l:patterns/hexcasting#autumnfloods:slot)$(thing)specified slot's/$ item can write iota, writes it.
miehex.entry.af_stack.desc1: Takes the first vector as the starting coordinate vector. If the boolean is false, takes the second vector as the coordinate vector, and returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks passed through by the line connecting the two coordinates. $(br2)If the boolean is true, takes the second vector as the direction vector, and returns a list of coordinate vectors of a certain number of blocks passed through by the coordinate vector along the direction vector, with the number equal to the integer value of the vector's magnitude.
miehex.advice.af_square_block.desc: Determines a cube with a vector and a positive integer, returns a list of coordinate vectors of the cube's twelve edges, or six faces, or blocks within it.
miehex.entry.af_stack.desc2: Takes a coordinate vector as the center coordinate of the cube, and a positive integer as half the side length of the cube. If the boolean is true, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks in the cube. $(br2)If the boolean is false, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks on the cube's faces; if null, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks on the cube's twelve edges.
miehex.advice.af_rectangle_block.desc: Determines a cube with two vectors, returns a list of coordinate vectors of the cube's twelve edges, or six faces, or blocks within it.
miehex.entry.af_stack.desc3: Takes two coordinate vectors as the coordinates of the two opposite vertices of the cube. If the boolean is true, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks in the cube. $(br2)If the boolean is false, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks on the cube's faces; if null, returns a list of coordinate vectors of all blocks on the cube's twelve edges.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc1: This page is used to record spells related to motes and transportation. For transportation spells, vec | [vec, vec] is used to specify the interaction face of the container. If it is a single position vector, it processes all items in all interaction faces of the container at that position vector; $(br2)if the container has different interaction faces, it can accept a list consisting of a position vector and any vector, and the latter vector will be processed as the axial unit vector with the smallest angle to it, that is, the normal vector pointing from the container center to the interaction face, processing all items in the specified interaction face of the container at that position vector.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc2: num | str | list is used to specify the matching method of items. num matches all items in the specified slot, str matches all items with the specified name, list consists of item name string and item NBT string, matches all items with the specified name and NBT. $(br2)num | bool represents the transfer logic. num will first try to transfer to the specified slot, True will first try to stack with items in the container. If it is False, or if there are still untransferred items after the first try, it will try to store in each slot in turn until the specified quantity is transferred, or all matching items, returning the total number transferred.
miehex.advice.af_get_contain.desc: $(br)Obtains specified information of the specified container interaction face or items in it in the specified way.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc3: If the third parameter is a boolean, it will return information about the items matched by the second parameter. True will return more comprehensive information of the item in the three parameters, different from the second parameter type; False will return more abstract information. $(br2)If the third parameter is null, it will only return corresponding information based on the $(l)nature/$ of the second parameter: if it is 0, returns a list of all slot numbers in the interaction face, positive numbers return non-empty slots, negative numbers return empty slots; str will return a list of item names of all non-empty slots in the interaction face; list will return a list of NBT of items in all non-empty slots in the interaction face.
miehex.advice.af_contain_contain.desc: $(br2)Transfers the specified quantity of specified items from the specified container to the specified container in the specified order.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc4: From the container interaction face specified by the first parameter, according to the matching method specified by the third parameter, transfer the items that meet the conditions to the container interaction face specified by the second parameter with the logic specified by the fourth parameter. $(br2)If during the transfer process, for a certain item among the matching items, the target container interaction face space is not enough to transfer all, only transfer the quantity that the interaction face can accommodate, then continue to process the next matching item until the quantity specified by the fifth parameter is transferred, or all items matching the third parameter, return the actual number of items transferred.
miehex.advice.af_mote_contain.desc: $(br)Transfers the specified quantity of specified items from the caster's bound motes to the specified container in the specified order.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc5: The matching method for motes is slightly different from containers, because it is difficult to obtain the index number of the mote record. Therefore, the matching of motes can no longer specify a certain slot, but can instead select a mote and match all items in it. $(br2)From the caster's bound mote hub, transfer to the container interaction face specified by the first parameter with the matching method specified by the second parameter and the logic specified by the third parameter, until the quantity specified by the fourth parameter is transferred, or all items matching the second parameter, return the actual number of items transferred.
miehex.advice.af_contain_mote.desc: $(br)Stores the specified quantity of specified items from the specified container into the caster's bound motes.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc6: From the container interaction face specified by the first parameter, according to the matching method specified by the second parameter, each stack of items that meet the conditions is sequentially converted into new motes and stored in the caster's bound motes, and will not automatically merge into existing motes. $(br2)When the remaining space in the motes is less than or equal to 1, the transfer will automatically stop. If there is enough space, it will continue until the quantity specified by the third parameter is transferred, or all items matching the second parameter. Like motes, logistics-related spells are not limited by casting range.
miehex.advice.af_motes.desc: Returns a list containing all motes in the currently bound hub.
miehex.advice.af_get_all_motes.desc: Returns a list containing the type strings of all motes in the currently bound hub.
miehex.advice.af_get_contained_motes.des: Returns a list containing all motes of the specified type in the currently bound hub.
miehex.advice.af_download.desc: Extracts the specified quantity of items from the specified mote and gives them to the caster.
miehex.advice.af_cloud.desc: Converts the items in the specified slot into motes and stores them in the bound hub.
miehex.advice.af_recipes.desc: Accepts an item name and returns a list of all crafting recipe strings for that item.
miehex.advice.af_restock.desc: Makes the specified villager restock, consuming 100 media points.
miehex.advice.af_merge.desc: Moves the two specified trades from the former villager to the latter, and increases the latter's experience and proficiency, consuming 100,000 media points.
miehex.advice.af_recipe.desc: Accepts a string and a number, automatically obtains the required materials from the bound hub, and crafts according to the string. If the materials are sufficient, returns the motes obtained from the simulated crafting; if the materials are not sufficient for crafting, returns the missing raw materials.
miehex.entry.af_mote.desc7: The string is composed of item names or placeholders, separated by commas in English, and placeholders are represented by "*". Finally, it is divided into nine parts, and if there are less than nine, the remaining parts will be considered empty. The string will be converted into a three-dimensional array in $(l:patterns/spells/motes#hexal:mote/craft)$(action)crafting/$. If the raw materials in the bound hub are sufficient to craft the specified number of times, returns a list of motes composed of stacked crafted items; if not enough to craft the specified number of times, returns a list of raw material names. For example, the string "minecraft:diamond,minecraft:diamond,minecraft:diamond,*,minecraft:stick,*,*,minecraft:stick,*" will simulate the crafting of a diamond pickaxe.
miehex.category.ccrecipes.desc: By gathering scattered consciousness energy, you can create strange blocks and even extract actual matter from pure consciousness, which is almost a miracle.
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.amythst.desc1: Although my understanding of consciousness collection is not yet complete, I have discovered that some simple items can be created without even stripping consciousness. For example, collecting villagers' consciousness can easily produce amethyst blocks, which can be cut on a cutting board to make media. Another example is that collecting both allay and villager consciousness can easily produce quenched crystal blocks. I just need to keep them in captivity and give them some healing from time to time, and I can easily obtain media - this still doesn't sound very ethical, but it's much more humane than stripping consciousness, isn't it?
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.villager.desc: Accepts a list of 1, 3, or 7 entity iotas, waits for 50 seconds, 5 seconds, and 0.5 seconds respectively, consumes a fixed small amount of media, and deals 15 points of damage to the entity
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.allay.desc: Only accepts a list of entity iotas consisting of 1 villager and 1 allay, waits for 10 seconds, consumes one charged amethyst, and deals 18 points of damage to the entity
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.amythst.desc2: If we need to be moral to these friendly creatures, then we don't need to show any mercy to those who are hostile to me, but maybe I can still give them a chance to live by returning good for evil... Collecting the consciousness of witches or evokers can get lapis lazuli blocks, and if we make good use of this special mineral, we can probably create very good items.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.witch.desc: Waits for 10 seconds, consumes a small amount of media, and deals 10 points of damage to the entity
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.evoker.desc: Waits for 5 seconds, consumes a small amount of media, and deals 10 points of damage to the entity
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.pig2.desc: I don't understand, I don't understand, how can I properly gather the firm and hard will of these ancient warriors... It's useless to keep playing with these man-made imitations, I have to go deep into the Nether again to find real warriors...
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.netherite.desc1: After a great battle, I have deeply understood the tenacious will of these powerful warriors, so how can I apply this will?
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.piglin_brute.des: Accepts a list of two entity iotas, waits for 5 seconds, consumes one charged amethyst
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.netherite.desc2: With a dazzling golden light and a deafening sound, I got it. It looks like those strange metals I once found in the chests of bastion remnants. My use of upgrade templates has told me of their power. Surprisingly, as a block condensed from consciousness, it actually has an entity! To turn this will into a material I can actually use, I tried many materials to induce it to precipitate. Finally, I used the blackstone bricks with strange patterns carved in the bastion remnants, and it precipitated! Unfortunately, it didn't directly give me a netherite block, but turned into an ancient debris - a bit of a pity, but maybe it's enough.
A powerful block condensed from firm will. Right-clicking with chiseled blackstone bricks can precipitate it into ancient debris.
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.piglin.desc1: I accidentally gave some quenched crystals to a wandering zombified piglin, and to my surprise, its empty eyes slowly regained clarity! Then the rotten flesh on its body began to fall off, new flesh began to grow, and its zombification was cured! It turned back into a piglin! It all happened so quickly that when the newly born piglin raised its golden sword and charged at me, I only then reacted and turned around to run back to the portal.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.zombified_piglin: Right-clicking a zombified piglin with a quenched crystal can cure it, consuming 5 quenched crystal shards
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.piglin.desc2: Later I did some more research, and I'm convinced that as a pure blank consciousness, quenched crystals can be used to repair or enhance the consciousness of certain creatures, and even cause corresponding changes in the material world - this seems similar to how quenched crystals change under the guidance of other media forms.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.piglin.desc: Right-clicking a piglin with a quenched crystal will transform it into a piglin brute, consuming 15 quenched crystal shards
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.piglin.desc3: Next, maybe I should try to collect the firm will of this warrior... What kind of material would that be, I'm so looking forward to it...
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.ore.desc1: The ancients said: "Firm and strong, their will cannot be taken away". When I discovered that I could create consciousness iron by collecting iron golem consciousness, I understood this sentence more deeply. If I collect only one iron golem's consciousness at a time, I can get consciousness iron after 1 minute of waiting. But if I put three iron golem entity iotas into a list at once, I only need to wait 5 seconds.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.iron_golem.desc: Can accept a list of 1 entity iota or 3 entity iotas, consumes one or three amethyst dust, each target entity takes 15 points of damage
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.media_iron.desc: A strange block that is empty and glowing, resembling an iron block. Right-clicking with smooth stone can precipitate it into an iron block.
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.ore.desc2: If the iron golem's will is as firm as steel, then the consciousness of undead creatures like zombies is like rusted copper, but after the purification of consciousness collection, the copper obtained seems to be relatively clean. Provide 1 entity to wait 1 minute, provide 3 entities to wait 5 seconds
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.zombie.desc: Can accept a list of 1 entity iota or 3 entity iotas, fixedly consumes 1 amethyst dust, deals 15 points of damage to the target entity.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.drowned.desc: Using drowned will have a slightly shorter waiting time.
miehex.advice.ccrecipes.media_copper.des: A strange block that is empty and glowing, resembling a copper block. Right-clicking with smooth stone can precipitate it into a copper block.
miehex.entry.ccrecipes.ore.desc3: It is said that there exists a kind of powerful warrior in the Nether that has survived from ancient times. Perhaps powerful metals matching their identity can be extracted from their consciousness.
miehex.entry.other_brainsweep.desc1: Through some research, I have obtained some consciousness stripping recipes for powerful creatures. I'm curious if I will ever really use these recipes for these powerful creatures.
miehex.advice.brainsweep.ender_dragon.de: Consumes 256 charged amethysts, although I don't know why it doesn't actually make the powerful dragon lose consciousness
miehex.advice.brainsweep.wither.desc: Consumes 256 charged amethysts, this one can make the wither lose consciousness. It is said that ancient hexcasters would use this spell to keep withers in their homes to deter enemies.
miehex.advice.guide.desc: When you can't understand your research, you can also try using this pattern to ask a wise man who calls himself Prometheus, said to be a prophet. However, his consciousness seems to be trapped in this pattern and cannot leave, so he can only communicate with me through the pattern.
miehex.entry.enchant.desc1: I discovered that item enchantments can actually be abstracted to form Iotas. Using these Iotas, I can easily and conveniently use hexcraft to enchant items
miehex.advice.get_enchant.desc: Accepts an item entity and returns a list of iotas corresponding to all enchantments on it
miehex.advice.give_enchant.desc: Accepts an enchantment iota and an item entity, enchants that item, consuming media of amethyst dust with the cube of the enchantment level plus one amethyst shard
miehex.advice.enchant_add.desc: Accepts two enchantment iotas of the same type, adds their levels together, and returns a new high-level enchantment
miehex.advice.grow_up.desc: Accepts a living entity, consumes media of three amethyst dust, and makes it instantly adult.
miehex.advice.exchant_exchange.desc: Accepts two item entity iotas, exchanges the enchantments they have, or makes one item with enchantments lose its enchantments and another item without enchantments gain the same enchantments, consumes 1 charged amethyst
miehex.entry.lesser_gates.desc1: Lesser Gates are a simple way of teleportation. Although there are many limitations, it is still a good method when you haven't acquired superior knowledge.
miehex.advice.lesser_gate.desc: Accepts a vector within casting range, treats this vector as the destination for 'Lesser Gate Teleportation' until the end of this casting, consumes 5 amethyst shards
miehex.advice.lesser_gate_close.desc: Accepts an entity, teleports it to the position determined by 'Create Lesser Gate', consumes a small amount of media. If not determined in advance, it has no effect.
miehex.entry.world.desc1: The reality of this world doesn't always seem so 'real' and 'stable'. Hex spirits too far away from me seem to stop working, crops don't seem to grow much when I'm not at home, and whenever I look into the distance, the world always seems to be in a fog... Fortunately, I found a way to maintain 'reality'.
miehex.advice.chunkloader_permanent.desc: Anchor the reality of the given position - consumes 1 amethyst shard, permanently forces the chunk at the target position to load.
miehex.advice.entity_anchor.desc: Temporarily anchor the reality of the given position - consumes a small amount of media, temporarily loads the chunk at the target position for about 15 seconds
miehex.entry.inv.desc1: There are hexes that can manipulate your own inventory through consciousness and media. They rely on inventory indexes to confirm inventory slots. The hotbar is 0~8 from left to right, and the inventory is 9~35 from left to right, top to bottom. If you give a number beyond the index, maybe the items will be sent to a strange place and disappear.
miehex.advice.inventory_control.desc: Accepts two inventory indexes, swaps items in the corresponding slots of your own inventory, consumes a small amount of media. If your consciousness is light enough, you may not need to consume media.
miehex.advice.item_control.desc: Accepts an inventory index or an item entity, drops one item from the slot corresponding to the index, or fills the item entities into empty slots in your own inventory, consumes a small amount of media. If your consciousness is light enough, you may not need to consume media.
miehex.entry.inv.desc2: Manipulating your own inventory is indeed somewhat useless, but fortunately I found some patterns to modify other entities' inventories - they are not powerful enough, but maybe they will have surprising effects in battle.
miehex.advice.expelliarmus.desc: Accepts a living entity, makes it drop its held item, consumes one amethyst shard.
miehex.advice.puzzle.desc: Accepts a player and two inventory indexes, swaps items in the corresponding slots of their inventory, consumes one charged amethyst.
miehex.advice.resurrectionem.desc: "Crucified, dead, and buried. Descended into Hades; on the third day he rose again from the dead."
miehex.entry.wr.desc1: My greatest work, possessing powerful strength. It will change the surrounding terrain and biomes within the range determined by several numbers, centered on the given vector, and at the same time consume 64 biome essences in the off-hand to determine the biome
miehex.entry.wr.desc2: The first number is the radius of influence, the second is the y-coordinate of the lowest point of action, the third is the y-value of the highest generation point relative to the ground, and the fourth determines whether to only change the surface or let the transformation go deep underground. When true, the last two numbers have no actual meaning. Consumes 10 charged amethysts, and additionally consumes amethyst dust equal to the square of the radius plus the height number.
miehex.entry.wr.desc3: Biome essences are not as gentle as they seem, so sometimes this spell will fail, which will waste media and essences. End biome essences are particularly difficult to control. Despite this, this spell is still too powerful. To prevent it from being used by people with malicious intentions, maybe I should delete the stroke order...
miehex.advice.zone_entity_by_name.desc: Takes a position, maximum distance, and a string, returns a list of all entities with the same name as the string within a cube of the given distance centered at that position. If the provided string is a registry name, returns a list of entities with the same registry name as the string
miehex.advice.list_insert.desc: Adds the iota at stack index 0 to the beginning of the list at stack index 1, adds the iota at stack index 0 to the end of that list, and outputs the resulting list
miehex.advice.easy_thrust.desc: Accepts a list at stack index 0, a list at index 1, and a number at index 2. Inserts each element from the list at index 1 into the list at index 0, starting after the element at the given index. The rest of the elements in the original list at index 0 remain unchanged
miehex.advice.easy_extract.desc: Accepts a list at stack index 0, and two numbers at stack indexes 1 and 2. Returns a list consisting of the elements from the given list starting at the first number and totaling the second number of elements, as well as a list consisting of all remaining elements from the original list
miehex.advice.list_by_index.desc: Accepts a list and a list of its indices, returns a new list composed of all elements from the previous list at the corresponding indices.
miehex.advice.cube_type.desc: Accepts two position vectors and a string, returns a list of coordinates of all blocks with the same ID as the given string within the cube defined by the two position vectors
miehex.advice.cube_types.desc: Accepts two position vectors and a list of strings, returns a list of coordinates of all blocks with IDs matching any string in the given list within the cube defined by the two position vectors
